clue.text: Force into show presented by Rowan, Martin and John, when pinching top of saucy bird

indicators.note: the force letter is put into the middle of the show-plus-name string

parts.note: Rowan & Martin's Laugh-In was a 1960s American TV comedy sketch show
Jack is a traditional pet form of the name John
G is the physics symbol for the gravitational constant, a force

indicators.note: the word for when grips the next letter between its own letters

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An old TV comedy line-up sneaks a cheeky bird into their show.
explanation.walkthrough: Laugh-In was an American sketch show. 'into' puts the force letter between the show and the nickname, and 'pinching' has the word for 'when' grip the top of 'saucy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian kookaburra, a large kingfisher famous for its cackling call, is also called by this name: a specific example of a bird.

clue.text: Words from Omar Sharif notwithstanding, men grieving over me vow to get out of order

definitions.note: a famous couplet from Omar Khayyam's Rubaiyat in FitzGerald's translation

indicators.note: letters that get out of order are jumbled, so the seven fodder words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Despite the actor Omar Sharif's words, a crowd of mourners promise to riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Omar Sharif' leads you to the film star, but the Omar meant is the Persian poet Omar Khayyam; 'Sharif' is anagram fodder along with the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a quotation from the Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam, so it is literally words by that poet.

clue.text: Evil spirits behind this need three kings anticipating Birth to eat

indicators.note: the BC letters swallow the other pieces inside them

parts.note: BC, before Christ, covers the years before the Nativity
lack means need, as in 'want for nothing'
the Magi were the three wise men or kings at the Nativity

explanation.surface: A nativity scene: wise men arriving before the birth and needing food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' has the era abbreviation for 'anticipating Birth' swallow the words for need and the kings; 'Evil spirits behind this' reads as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery invoking demons is what malign spirits are said to drive, so the dark art is the thing they stand behind.

clue.text: Make offer for old puzzle

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
pose is an old word for a puzzling question, as in poser

explanation.surface: Someone bids on an antique jigsaw.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward a suggestion or a marriage offer is to make an offer, a plain synonym.

clue.text: See 2
See 2
It's time to make love — bonkers left at 22:16 hours (midweek)

indicators.note: bonkers means crazy, so the gathered letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
the solution to clue 22 across, given by cross-reference

indicators.note: sixteen hours is two thirds of a day, so only the latter two thirds of the day's name survive

parts.note: the middle day of the week is Wednesday

explanation.surface: A note says it is time for passion: crazy, leaving late on Wednesday night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bonkers' turns L + AT + INVEST into STVALENTI; '16 hours' keeps two thirds of WEDNESDAY, dropping WED to leave NESDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: February 14th is the lovers' festival, a date set aside for romance.

clue.text: A single composer (actually more than one) needs something to play back

parts.note: Bach names a whole family of composers, J S Bach and his sons

indicators.note: back tells us the word for a part is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an actor plays a role

explanation.surface: A solo composer, or several, needs a part to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried man is a single, so the noun means an unattached person.

clue.text: It's tipped in the object of an old Irish joke, and it doesn't happen very often!

indicators.note: the pronoun is poured into the joke's object as if tipped into a container

parts.words: the object of an old Irish joke
parts.note: the old joke reads 'It's a long way to Tipperary' as 'a long way to tip a rary', so the rary is what is tipped
it, with the 's as a joining is

explanation.surface: A gag about an Irish town is told so seldom it is a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke: 'It's a long way to Tipperary' heard as 'a long way to tip a rary', making a rary something to tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncommon, an event seldom seen, is a rare occurrence, so the clause describes it.

clue.text: Asexual trumpeter goes to clubs

parts.note: the agami is a South American heron, also called a trumpeter
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: An unromantic brass player heads off to the nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology the word describes reproduction without sexual union, a technical synonym.

clue.text: Condition — alien has it brought into the light, wanting to go back

indicators.note: the alien and the pronoun are placed inside the light word
this light is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a lamp is a light
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sci-fi creature is dragged towards a lamp and longs to go home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting to go back' reverses the light; 'brought into' sets the alien and 'it' inside it. The film alien's wish to go home colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild form of epilepsy is a medical condition.

clue.text: Capital brekkie visitors have

indicators.note: the visitors' words hold the answer within them, so the letters are taken from inside

explanation.surface: Guests in a capital city enjoy their morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Ukraine, an example of a national capital.

clue.text: Drunk has crash on big road, getting masses confused

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: the M1 motorway, written MI in crosswords
a slurred drunkard says 'smashes' with an extra h

explanation.surface: A drunk driver crashes on the motorway, leaving people in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's first long motorway, London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbled heaps or confused collections are hotchpotches, so the noun means masses in disorder.

clue.text: Holding group up to begin with, Malingering Git is making complaint

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken
in a down answer, up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a group of nine, like a nonet
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lazy layabout skiving off his group fakes illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the group of nine in this down answer; 'Holding' puts it inside the opening letter of 'Malingering'.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint is a general word for an illness, and this brain infection is an example of one.

clue.text: Illustrations describe, from right to left, summons for dinner and drinks

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around it, so the examples enclose the other piece

parts.note: e.g. means for example, so illustrations are EGs

indicators.note: this word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a gong is struck to call people to dinner

explanation.surface: Pictures show, in reverse order, the call to dinner and the cocktails.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a sweet egg-and-cream drink, so its plural is an example of drinks.

clue.text: In one, one applies for University … that's senseless!

indicators.note: one item applies in place of another, so it replaces it

parts.note: taken as written
unity is oneness, as in 'in unity'
A as the indefinite article means one

explanation.surface: Applying to university as one of many is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applies for' puts A where the U of INUNITY was, giving INANITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolishness or pointlessness is the quality of something senseless, the noun form of the idea.

clue.text: See 2
Own 2 and 6

definitions.meaning: these three letters are the latter part of the five-letter word for royal headgear, so the word is roughly a portion of it
two shillings and sixpence, the value of an old British coin

explanation.walkthrough: Before decimal currency in 1971, Britain had a coin worth two shillings and sixpence, written 2/6.
explanation.definitionFit: The old coin worth two shillings and six pence carried this name, and o-w-n is the tail of the regal headwear.

clue.text: Applause for producer

definitions.meaning: a round of clapping, as in 'give them a big one'
a worker, as in a farm labourer or factory worker who makes things

explanation.definitionFit: Clapping is called giving someone a big one of these, and a farm worker is also called by the same word.

clue.text: What cheats do like fleecing top man?

indicators.note: the word for like is wrapped around the ruler as a fleece wraps a sheep

parts.note: same means like, identical
a king is the top man of a realm

explanation.surface: Do con artists enjoy swindling the boss?
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle or rigged racket is what cheats run, so the phrase names their activity.

clue.text: A male voice, all things considered — get her out!

indicators.note: these words are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: altogether means all things considered, on the whole
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man with a high voice shouts to have a woman removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest adult male singing voice, the countertenor range, goes by this name.

clue.text: Put one's shirt and underwear on

parts.note: in means on, wearing, as in 'in a hat'
a vest is an undershirt

explanation.surface: Get dressed: shirt and underclothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'put one's shirt on' a horse is a British idiom for betting everything on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Staking one's money on something is putting money into it, so the idiom matches committing funds.

clue.text: What a tracker-dog follows, going back in time

definitions.meaning: a dog trails a smell, read as two words
tracing a family line back through ancestors

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into A and SCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: In genealogy one traces ancestry upward, so moving to earlier generations is a climb through the family tree.

clue.text: Stupid relation from Japan?

indicators.note: something stupid is muddled, so the letters of relation are scrambled

explanation.definitionFit: Japan is in the Far East, so a person or thing from there is Eastern; the question mark marks it as an example.
